subject: Urgent: Production 5xx surge + timeouts affecting ShopFast checkout
messages:
From: Maya Bronson <maya@shopfast.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@shopfast.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: Checkout failures in production (5xx / timeouts)

Hi Laura —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx and timeout errors at ~07:50 PDT. Our checkout rate dropped by ~40% and customers are reporting failed payments. The logs show a flood of 503/504 responses coming from your API gateway and then client-side retries that amplify the issue. We rolled a config revert on our end (no change).

Key notes:
- Peaks at ~07:58–08:05 PDT, sustained elevated error-rate for ~20m
- Error samples attached (error_snapshot_0615.png) and a few trace ids: 3f1a-7c9b, 3f1a-7d0a
- We are live on us-west1 for primary traffic, with failover to us-west2 but failover didn't kick cleanly

This is high-severity for us — revenue is impacted. Please triage immediately and loop in anyone needed on your side. We need an ETA and mitigation plan.

— Maya

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 08:45:36 -0700
Subject: Re: URGENT: Checkout failures in production (5xx / timeouts)

Laura — quick summary of findings from gateway + network traces:

- Observed a surge of upstream 502/503 responses originating from connections to our ILB in us-west1. The timing correlates with an upstream GCP egress networking degradation (packet loss + connection resets) reported in us-west1.
- The gateway attempted retries per normal client settings; however, many customer SDK instances do immediate retries which, combined with the gateway retries, produced retry amplification (multiplexed retry storms) and exhausted worker queues.
- DNS observations: a subset of our routes were resolving to an older, unhealthy backend IP due to delayed DNS TTL propagation from a third-party DNS provider (nm-dns). That caused a fraction of traffic to hit degraded hosts even after failover was triggered.

Immediate mitigation recommended (short-term):
1) Pause internal gateway retries for checkout routes for 30 minutes (to avoid amplification).
2) Push a control-plane policy to route traffic away from us-west1 to us-west2 as a soft-failover (sticky sessions considered).
3) Ask ShopFast to temporarily throttle automatic client retries (we can provide a runtime knob for their SDK).
4) Coordinate with nm-dns to purge stale DNS entries for the service host — I’ve opened a ticket, cc nm-dns.

I’ve attached a short mitigation plan with steps (mitigation_plan_20260615.pdf) and a diagnosis log snippet (error_snapshot_0615.log). I’ll start the route reconfiguration once we have Laura's sign-off.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Infrastructure
marcus_lin@redwood.com

- Technical ETA: 15–25 minutes for soft-failover, then another 10m to observe error rates fall.
- We will provide a post-incident timeline and root-cause analysis within 48 hours.

Action items for ShopFast: please enable client-side backoff on the SDK (we can supply a temporary patch) and share the full list of trace ids if possible.
